data.narrative:
Generalist AI is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Pete Florence (ex-DeepMind, co-creator of PaLM-E and RT-2), Andy Zeng (ex-DeepMind Chief Scientist), and Andrew Barry (ex-Boston Dynamics CTO). The company has raised $500M+ to date and carries a current post-money valuation of $2.0B. The valuation universe comprises five private robotics peers at Series A through Series C stages plus one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier from the $2.0B Series B base, implying $3.8B at the next funding stage. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector comparables—Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), Humanoid ($1.4B Series A), Agile Robots ($1.0B Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B Series C)—yields a median valuation of $1.4B with a range of $1.0B to $1.8B. The stage-progression method typically reflects founder pedigree and capital efficiency; the peer-median approach anchors to observable market pricing.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $1.1B to $4.4B, with a median of $2.6B. The current $2.0B valuation sits below the triangulated median, positioning it within the lower-middle of the supported range. Key uncertainties include stage-specific forward multiples in a market segment with limited public comparables and the degree to which founder credentials command a valuation premium relative to peer cohort median.
